name: two-word thesis hook with path diagram
looks: Two single words hard-cut onto the screen in sequence, bracketed on a dark field. The first arrives clean; the second drops in through a heavy motion blur that resolves as it lands. A beat later a tiny diagram appears: a dot and a small square joined by a wavering connecting line, with a one-line caption underneath naming that line as the short route between the two ideas the words named.
build: Two DOM word cards hard-cut on the beat, no crossfade (the kinetic-word-run mechanic); the second word's entrance uses a directional motion-blur filter that clears on arrival. The diagram is two DOM/SVG nodes joined by an SVG path stroked on via strokeDashoffset, with a slow sine wobble on its control point; the caption clips in beneath.
sound: A hit on each word's cut, a whoosh under the blurred word's entrance, a quiet tick as the connecting line draws.
prompt: Hard-cut a two-word thesis statement onto the screen, one clean, one arriving through a heavy motion blur that resolves as it lands, then follow it with a tiny node-and-line diagram that names the straight line between the two ideas the words set up. Keep both words and the diagram on the beat, with no crossfades.
